places.title: Place de la Bourse and the Miroir d’eau
places.architect: Jacques and Ange-Jacques Gabriel; Michel Corajoud, Pierre Gangnet and Jean-Max Llorca (Miroir d’eau)
places.why: The royal square that opened the medieval city to the river: a U of pale limestone palaces facing the Garonne. In front of it a granite slab under two centimetres of water mirrors the facades, then turns into a sheet of mist.

photos.file: 139 - Place de la Bourse et le miroir d'eau - Bordeaux.jpg
photos.author: Patrick Despoix

photos.file: Le miroir d'eau à Bordeaux en septembre 2017.jpg
photos.author: AlineRockstud68

photos.file: Miroir d'eau et place de la Bourse (Bordeaux) (2).jpg
photos.author: Gzen92

places.title: The quays of the Garonne (Port of the Moon)
places.why: Four kilometres of 18th-century stone facades curving along the crescent of the river. The port sheds were cleared for a continuous riverside promenade with lawns, gardens, cycle lanes and the tram.

places.title: Cathédrale Saint-André, Tour Pey-Berland and Place Pey-Berland
places.why: A Gothic cathedral with a long nave and twin spires, and its bell tower standing apart across the square, topped by a gilded Virgin. The square around them was cleared of traffic and repaved as one stone floor.

photos.file: Bordeaux Église Saint-Michel Flèche Saint-Michel Vue sur la Cathédrale Saint-André 2.jpg
photos.author: Zairon

places.title: Grand Théâtre and Place de la Comédie
places.why: A neoclassical opera house fronted by twelve Corinthian columns carrying statues of the Muses and goddesses. Its grand staircase was a model for the Paris Opéra; the square in front is the city’s main crossroads.

places.title: Basilique Saint-Michel and its spire
places.why: A Flamboyant Gothic basilica with a free-standing bell tower, the tallest spire in southern France at 114 m. The square below fills with a flea market at weekends.

photos.author: Image details Casio EX ZR1000 Orikrin1998 CC-BY-3.0

places.title: Porte Cailhau
places.why: A 35 m city gate on the riverside, half fortress and half triumphal arch, built to celebrate a royal victory in Italy. Its pointed turrets and machicolations face the quay.

photos.file: 🇫🇷 🇪🇺 Puerta de Cailhau (Burdeos, Francia, 1-3-2008) - Flickr - Juanje Orío.jpg
photos.author: Juanje Orío from Logroño, España (Europa)

places.title: Grosse Cloche
places.why: The belfry of the medieval town hall: two round towers with conical roofs framing a clock and a bell of almost eight tonnes, straddling Rue Saint-James.

places.title: Saint-Pierre quarter
places.why: The medieval core between the cathedral and the river: narrow car-free lanes of limestone houses opening onto small squares with café terraces, around a Gothic church.

places.title: Esplanade des Quinconces and the Monument aux Girondins
places.why: One of the largest city squares in Europe, laid out on the site of a demolished royal fortress and opening onto the river between two rostral columns. At its head stands a fountain column crowned by Liberty, with bronze horses rearing from the basin.

places.title: Pont de pierre
places.why: The first bridge across the Garonne in the city: seventeen brick and stone arches with lamps along the parapet. Now reserved for trams, bikes and pedestrians, it is the best place to see the curve of the quays.

photos.file: Bordeaux - Pont de Pierre vu depuis la flèche Saint Michel V2.jpg
photos.author: Guallendra

places.title: Rue Sainte-Catherine
places.why: The old Roman north–south axis, now a 1.2 km pedestrian shopping street running from the Grand Théâtre to Place de la Victoire past the city’s busiest corners.

places.title: Chartrons
places.why: The old wine merchants’ quarter north of the centre: stone townhouses and cellars behind the quay, antique shops along Rue Notre-Dame, a market hall and a Sunday market on the riverfront.

photos.file: La Patine du Temps, Bordeaux, July 2014 (01).JPG
photos.author: Ardfern

places.title: La Cité du Vin
places.why: A curving 55 m tower of glass and gold-toned aluminium on the riverbank, shaped to suggest wine swirling in a glass. The exhibition on wine culture ends in a belvedere at the top.

places.title: Jardin Public
places.why: The city’s historic garden, first laid out in the French style and remade as an English landscape park with a winding stream, lawns and old trees, behind wrought-iron gates and an arcaded terrace.

places.title: Palais Rohan and the Musée des Beaux-Arts
places.architect: Joseph Étienne and Richard-François Bonfin; Charles Burguet (museum wings)
places.why: The archbishop’s neoclassical palace, now the city hall, with a cour d’honneur on Place Pey-Berland. Its garden leads to the two wings of the fine arts museum.

photos.file: 00 2676 Hôtel de ville de Bordeaux (Palais Rohan).jpg
photos.author: W. Bulach

places.title: Marché des Capucins
places.why: The covered food market locals call the belly of Bordeaux: stalls of fish, cheese and wine, and oyster bars open from early morning.

photos.file: Bordeaux - Marché des Capucins - Entrée nord.jpg
photos.author: Romainbehar

places.title: Allées de Tourny and Cours de l’Intendance
places.why: The 18th-century heart of the Golden Triangle: a wide promenade of plane trees and a straight shopping street lined with uniform stone facades, laid out when the medieval walls came down.

photos.file: Allées de Tourny à Bordeaux, vues depuis la Maison du Vin, 2022.jpg
photos.author: Jefunky

photos.file: Jean-Jacques Bel - Hôtel particulier, allées de Tourny (Bordeaux).jpg
photos.author: William Ellison

places.title: MÉCA — Maison de l’économie créative et de la culture
places.why: A single loop of pale perforated concrete by the river that frames a view of the Garonne: the riverside promenade passes through the arch and climbs stepped terraces up into the building.

photos.file: La MECA - Bordeaux - Flickr - Patrice Puig.jpg
photos.author: Patrice Puig from le teich

places.title: Tribunal judiciaire (Law Courts)
places.why: Seven cedar-clad courtrooms shaped like wine vats sit on concrete legs inside a glass hall under a wavy copper roof, beside the towers of the medieval Fort du Hâ.

photos.file: Palais de justice de Bordeaux, July 2014 (01).JPG
photos.author: Ardfern

photos.file: Bordeaux Cathédrale Saint-André Tour Pey-Berland Vue sur le Palais de Justice.jpg
photos.author: Zairon

places.title: Fort du Hâ and the École nationale de la magistrature
places.why: Two round towers of a 15th-century fortress kept inside the concrete buildings of the national school for judges, next to Rogers’ courts: three eras of justice on one block.

points.name: Tour nord du Fort du Hâ

photos.file: Escuela Nacional de la Magistratura de Francia.jpg
photos.author: Pablohn6

places.title: Matmut Atlantique (Nouveau Stade de Bordeaux)
places.why: A 42,000-seat stadium under a sharp rectangular roof held up by a forest of thin white columns, a nod to the pines of the Landes. Open stairs wrap the stands.

photos.file: Vue aerienne Nouveau stade - parc des expos Bordeaux.jpg
photos.author: Prométhée33

places.title: Pont Simone-Veil
places.architect: OMA (Rem Koolhaas, Chris van Duijn) with Michel Desvigne
places.why: A low, 44 m wide concrete bridge where more than half of the deck is left as open public space for walking, markets and events rather than traffic.

places.title: Pont Jacques-Chaban-Delmas
places.architect: Michel Virlogeux (engineer); Charles and Thomas Lavigne
places.why: A vertical-lift bridge whose central deck rises between four slender towers to let tall ships through to the quays. Lit from inside the towers at night.

photos.file: Bordeaux Cité du Vin Vue sur le Pont Jacques-Chaban-Delmas 2.jpg
photos.author: Zairon

places.title: Arkéa Arena
places.why: A concert arena wrapped in white concrete like a smooth pebble on the riverbank, at the end of the Simone-Veil bridge.

places.title: Musée Mer Marine
places.why: A maritime museum by the wet docks in a long white building shaped like a moored ship.

places.title: Entrepôt Lainé — CAPC and arc en rêve
places.architect: Claude Deschamps; Denis Valode and Jean Pistre with Andrée Putman (conversion)
places.why: A warehouse for colonial goods whose vast nave of stone arches and timber beams now holds the contemporary art museum and the city’s architecture centre.

places.title: Gare Saint-Jean
places.architect: Marius Toudoire and Louis Choron; Daydé & Pillé (train shed)
places.why: The railway station of 1898: a stone façade with a clock tower in front of an iron and glass train shed 300 m long, once the largest in Europe.

places.title: Musée d’Aquitaine
places.why: The history museum of Bordeaux and its region, from Gallo-Roman sculpture to the city’s role in the Atlantic slave trade, in the former faculty of letters.

places.title: Basilique Saint-Seurin
places.why: A pilgrimage church on the Way of St James with a Romanesque-Gothic body, a carved south porch and a crypt of Merovingian sarcophagi above an early Christian necropolis.

places.title: Palais Gallien
places.why: The brick and stone arcades of a 2nd-century Roman amphitheatre, standing in a garden among 18th-century houses.

places.title: Abbatiale Sainte-Croix
places.why: A Romanesque abbey church with a richly carved west front of arches, capitals and sculpted vices.

places.title: Église Notre-Dame
places.why: A baroque church modelled on the Jesuit Gesù in Rome, with a sculpted façade facing a small square and a courtyard of arcades behind.

places.title: Grande synagogue
places.why: One of the largest synagogues in Europe, set back behind a courtyard; its vaulted prayer hall hangs from an iron frame made in Gustave Eiffel’s workshops.

places.title: Hangar 14
places.why: A 1930 port shed on the Chartrons quay converted into an exhibition and event hall, wrapped in a translucent skin facing the river promenade.

places.title: Pôle universitaire de sciences de gestion
places.why: Lacaton & Vassal’s management school on the right bank: four buildings raised around a square, with passageways and courtyards on different levels, next to the botanical garden.

places.title: Bourse du Travail
places.why: An Art Deco labour hall by the city architect, with carved reliefs and painted murals by Alfred Janniot, Jean Dupas and other artists.

photos.file: Bordeaux Bourse du Travail art déco le péristyle.JPG
photos.author: Langladure

photos.file: Bordeaux Bourse du Travail fresque de Camille de Buzon 2.JPG
photos.author: Langladure

places.title: Stade Chaban-Delmas
places.why: An Art Deco stadium built for the 1938 World Cup, the first in the world with covered stands free of any supporting pillar.

places.title: Hôtel Saint-James
places.why: A hotel and restaurant on the hills above the river, made of rusted-steel pavilions shaped like tobacco-drying barns among the vines.

places.title: Base sous-marine (Bassins des Lumières)
places.why: A German U-boat bunker 245 m long with eleven pens under a roof several metres thick. The raw concrete halls now host immersive digital art shows.

places.title: Darwin (Caserne Niel)
places.why: Former military barracks on the right bank turned into a working ecosystem of start-ups, a skate hall, an organic canteen and street art, kept rough rather than restored.

places.title: Mériadeck
places.architect: Jean Royer (plan); Edmond Lay, Pierre Layré-Cassou and Pierre Dugravier (Caisse d’épargne)
places.why: A modernist business district built on a raised slab over a cleared working-class neighbourhood: office towers and gardens above the street, and the stepped brutalist savings bank at its entrance.

places.title: Cité administrative
places.why: Bordeaux’s first real skyscraper: a slim government office tower of the early 1970s that still marks the western skyline.

places.title: Caserne des pompiers de la Benauge
places.why: A post-war fire station on the right bank: a long block of firemen’s flats with coloured panels raised over the engine garages, in the spirit of Le Corbusier. Being converted to new uses.

photos.file: Bordeaux caserne des pompiers de la Benauge.JPG
photos.author: Guallendra

places.title: Maison à Bordeaux (Villa Lemoine)
places.why: A hillside house for a wheelchair user built around a room-sized lifting platform that moves between three floors; a heavy concrete box floats over a glass living level.
places.note: Private home behind trees; not visible from the road.

places.title: UCPA Sport Station
places.why: Sports fields stacked like streets and squares on open concrete floors wrapped in windbreak netting: climbing, padel, a skate park and a golf range on the roof.

places.title: Conservatoire Jacques-Thibaud
places.why: A brutalist music school with a heavily ribbed concrete façade next to the Romanesque abbey of Sainte-Croix.

photos.file: Conservatoire à rayonnement régional de Bordeaux.JPG
photos.author: Jean-Louis Lascoux

places.title: Cité du Grand Parc
places.architect: Lacaton & Vassal, Frédéric Druot, Christophe Hutin (530 dwellings); Bernard Bühler (Arc-en-Ciel)
places.why: A 1960s estate of slab blocks where three buildings got a new skin of winter gardens and balconies while tenants stayed at home, turning each flat into a light-filled house in the sky. At the estate entrance, the Arc-en-Ciel social housing wraps a curve in coloured glass fins.

points.name: Buildings G, H and I — 530 transformed dwellings
Salle des fêtes du Grand Parc

places.title: Bassins à flot
places.why: The former wet docks turned into a new quarter: blocks of flats by many architects with rooftop gardens and varied heights around the water, next to warehouses, an old garage and the submarine base.

photos.file: Bordeaux - Bassins à flot - Oz Boat - Vue sur le quai du Maroc.jpg
photos.author: Romainbehar

places.title: Ginko eco-district
places.why: A new district by the lake built block by block around canals, rain gardens and a park, with a pedestrian shopping street over underground parking and a tram line to the centre.

photos.file: Canal du Parc Bühler à Bordeaux sous la neige.jpg
photos.author: TottoB

places.title: Génicart estate renovation
places.why: A 1960s estate of towers on the right-bank hills renovated rather than demolished: new balconies and facades for 709 homes and car-free green walks and play spaces between them.

places.title: Cité Frugès
places.why: An early experiment in standardised housing for factory workers: some fifty cubic houses with roof terraces, arcades and walls painted brown, blue and green. One house is open as a museum.

places.title: Maison Latapie
places.why: An inexpensive family house doubled by a greenhouse of corrugated polycarbonate that opens in summer, the first manifesto of Lacaton & Vassal’s more space for less.
places.note: Private home; view from the street.

places.title: Jardin botanique de la Bastide
places.why: A botanical garden laid out as a strip of landscapes of the region, with fields of crops, water gardens and cracked rock islands, facing the historic city across the river.

places.title: Parc aux Angéliques
places.why: A long riverside park on the right bank planted in strips of trees and meadows, with the best view of the Port of the Moon facades opposite.

places.title: Place du Parlement
places.why: A small, enclosed 18th-century square of matching facades with carved masks and wrought-iron balconies around a fountain, filled with café tables.

places.title: Place de la Victoire
places.why: The student square at the south end of Rue Sainte-Catherine, with an 18th-century triumphal gate, a tall red marble column with bronze turtles and busy terraces.

places.title: Parc Bordelais
places.why: A 28 ha 19th-century landscape park of old trees, a winding river and lawns, where west Bordeaux comes to walk and picnic.

photos.file: Parc Bordelais, Bordeaux, Aquitaine, France - panoramio (1).jpg
photos.author: M.Strīķis

places.title: Parc Rivière
places.why: A quiet former merchant’s estate with lawns, old trees, a gardener’s house and a greenhouse, between the Chartrons and the Grand Parc.

photos.author: Grand Parc - Bordeaux, France from France
Grand Parc - Bordeaux, France from France

places.title: Parc de Bourran
places.why: An 18 ha landscape park around a château in Mérignac, with rolling lawns, water and old trees on a former wine estate.

places.title: Parc de Majolan
places.why: A 19th-century folly park with artificial grottoes, islands, rock bridges and a lake, listed as a remarkable garden of France.

places.title: Parc Palmer
places.why: A hillside park on the right bank with wide views across the city and the river, around a château and the Rocher de Palmer music venue.

places.title: Parc de l’Ermitage
places.why: A wild park on the Lormont hillside around an old hermitage and quarries, with viewpoints over the river, the Port of the Moon and the Pont d’Aquitaine.
